analysis.title: GS FINS & REITs Daily
key_insights: Overnight: E-minis -30bps, Nasdaq futures -15bps, US 10-year yield higher at 4.98%, crude +1%. The global AI trade is showing some stabilization, though not extremely convincing, after the prior day's sell-off.
The desk's HF Popular Pair Basket (GSTHVIPP) finished down 4.2% on 10/22, its worst move since 2011.
In the pre-market DRAM is +2.5% and SMH +50bps. Overnight Hynix was +4%, Samsung +40bps and Tokyo Electron flat. AI-related names that reported last night: WDC -2% pre, BE -2.5%, FIX -2%, MXL +4%.
Europe is lower (FTSE -60bps, DAX -1%, CAC -80bps) on mixed PMIs (France worse, Germany mixed, UK better). Kering is down 12% and Volvo Car down 25% after results. Asia closed mostly higher.

The S&P Financial Index closed +1.18% last session, +5.6% above its 200DMA with a 14d RSI of 63. 79% of S&P Financial stocks rose. Alts, Mortgage and Info Services outperformed. Consumer Fins, Traditional AMs and E-Brokers lagged.
Last session's market levels: 2yr yield -17bps at 4.64%, 10yr -17bps at 4.96%, 30yr -13bps at 5.28%, VIX +14% at 19, MOVE +11% at 107, Bitcoin -4% at 81.2k, IG CDX +3% at 63, HY CDX +3% at 360.

AXP: the desk rates the print negative to neutral (-/=). Revenue ex NII was weaker and the earnings beat was lower quality, largely driven by reserve release. Billings grew +7.8% against the +8% the company cited at Barclays in September, and the market had expected accelerating spend. VCE was in line with the Street and expenses were well managed. The October spend commentary, VCE trajectory into 2027 and early 2027 guide on the 8:30am call are the things to watch. The stock can do well if management is positive on VCE trajectory.

FCNCA: the desk is positive (+). Solid beat and raise on strong growth. PPNR beat on better NII and core fees. NIM of 3.07% missed consensus 3.10% by 3bp. The 4Q guide implies NII of $1.70-1.77bn vs consensus $1.71bn, fees of $540-580mn vs $546mn and expenses of $1.35-1.39bn vs $1.36bn.

SLM: the desk is negative (-). EPS was -$0.19 against a Street estimate of +$0.17. The miss came from higher provisions (NCO guide raised), higher marketing opex, and lower NII and NIM. Originations were strong and the Sixth Street partnership was finalized. The desk says investor sentiment is unforgiving of outliers on credit.

Mortgage insurers are in focus after a Trump executive order directing the FHFA director to create a pilot program that proactively cancels borrowers' mortgage insurance premiums once equity requirements are met on current market value. Investors are assessing in-force policy cancellations and the earnings impact.

Prime book data: more than two-thirds of hedge funds finished down on 10/22 as concentrated shorts were squeezed. All three broad equity strategies fell more than 1% on the same day for the first time since COVID. Global Fundamental L/S was -1.4% (-2.1 SD), its worst day since July 16. Global Systematic L/S was -1.3% (-3.4 SD), the third-worst day since December 2023. Multi-Strats were -1.9% (-3.2 SD), the second-worst day since the April 2025 tariff sell-off behind July 28.

Unconstrained Momentum (GSPRHIMO) is in its worst drawdown since the GFC, excluding the Covid period. A related GS note says the High Beta Momentum Pair has erased all YTD gains and is back to September lows.

Real estate: towers are +5-7% pre-market on reports that SpaceX is in talks to access 80,000 cell sites for a new network. KRC reported FFO of 88c, 1c above the Street, and narrowed FY26 FFO guidance with the midpoint up 1c to $3.57.

Global Economics Analyst: under a baseline 15% AI-driven productivity increase, up to 9% of US workers could be temporarily displaced, with slower hiring weighing on employment by an additional 3%. Each 1pp of productivity raises unemployment by 0.3-0.4pp temporarily. Only 23% of US establishments use AI in regular workflows.

Global Credit Trader: risks to year-end spread forecasts are tilted toward more widening. USD spreads are expected to moderately overshoot the March 2026 peaks of 93bp for IG and 335bp for HY. North America strategic M&A is at a record $1.3 trillion YTD, and M&A-related supply is $177bn in USD IG and $55bn in USD HY.

sector_views.rationale: The sector rose 1.18% and sits 5.6% above its 200DMA. Alts, mortgage and info services outperformed while consumer finance, traditional asset managers and e-brokers lagged.
Towers rallied pre-market on the SpaceX cell site report. KRC leasing is strong in the Bay Area.

earnings_insights: AXP reported 3Q earnings, a beat the desk calls lower quality and largely driven by reserve release. Billings grew +7.8%. Revenue ex NII was weaker than expected. The call is at 8:30am.

FCNCA reported 3Q, a beat and raise. NIM was 3.07% reported vs 3.10% consensus. 4Q guide: NII $1.70-1.77bn vs consensus $1.71bn, fees $540-580mn vs consensus $546mn, expenses $1.35-1.39bn vs consensus $1.36bn. The call is at 9am.
SLM reported EPS of -$0.19 vs Street estimate of +$0.17. Drivers were higher provisions with a raised NCO guide, higher marketing opex, and lower NII and NIM.

KRC reported 3Q26 FFO of 88c vs Street 87c. FY26 FFO guidance was narrowed with the midpoint up 1c to $3.57. 3Q26 leasing was 815k sqft of signed new and renewal leases, +117% QoQ and +48% YoY. Leasing spreads were +30.6% GAAP and +9.7% cash. The call is at 1pm.
Pre-market earnings on 10/23 include ALV, AXP, BAH and SLB. AI-related names that reported the prior night: WDC, BE, FIX, MXL.
